Now I have a complete picture of all files. Let me create run_parallel_all.sh:
Here's what run_parallel_all.sh does and how it maps to your existing infrastructure:
Wave structure (mirrors ci_parallel_schedule_simplify.yml and parallel_dispatch_dag.svg):
Wave	Experiments	Execution
1	exp1	Sequential — instability needs its JSON output
2+3	exp1b, exp2_feynman, exp2, hybrid_all_domains, exp3, exp3b, extrap, suppA, suppB, suppB_sc	Parallel background processes (throttled by --jobs N, default 11)
4	instability	Sequential — after Wave 1
5	tables + figures	Parallel pair
6	validate	Sequential
Key design choices:
    • Delegates everything to run_all.sh --step <exp> — no logic is duplicated, all your existing fixes (FIX-D1 through FIX-suppA-5, etc.) are automatically inherited. 
    • Wave 2+3 uses wait on background PIDs with a MAX_JOBS throttle so you don't overwhelm the machine. A 2-second stagger between launches avoids filesystem/API bursts. 
    • Wave 1 failure is non-fatal for Wave 2+3 (they're independent), but a warning is emitted and instability (Wave 4) is still attempted so you get a partial run. 
    • Every experiment gets its own log at <RESULTS_DIR>/parallel_run_wave<N>_<exp>.log, plus a consolidated parallel_run_summary.log. 
Usage examples:
bash
# Full pipeline
./run_parallel_all.sh

# Resume from Wave 4 (exp1 and Wave 2+3 already done)
./run_parallel_all.sh --from wave4

# Skip exp1 (results already committed), run everything else
./run_parallel_all.sh --skip-wave1

# Dry run to preview commands
./run_parallel_all.sh --dry-run

# Cap to 4 parallel jobs (e.g. on a smaller machine)
./run_parallel_all.sh --jobs 4
